A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Grandmother is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Grandmother** is an analog, **semi-modular**, 32-key synth by **Moog Music**, with circuits based on the Moog modular and the Minimoog (Wikipedia, "Moog Grandmother"). Its manual is dated 2018.
- Semi-modular: it plays without cables, and patch cables can change the path (Wikipedia).
- It cannot save sounds: you draw them on patch sheets instead (Wikipedia), like the [Model D](intro-model-d.qmd).

## Its sound

- **Two oscillators**: triangle, saw, square or narrow pulse (Grandmother manual, PDF pp. 11-12).
- A **ladder low-pass filter**, 24 dB (manual, PDF pp. 16-17), and a separate 1-pole **high-pass** you can patch in (PDF p. 7, 15).
- A real **spring reverb** inside (manual, PDF p. 21).
- One ADSR envelope (manual, PDF pp. 18-19).

## The panel

This is the Grandmother panel from [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). Play it from the keys under the panel, the computer keys (a w s e d f t g y h u j k) or a MIDI keyboard. Turn any knob while you play. The sound is this site's own model; nobody has compared it with the real instrument.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a worked example and changes one thing.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="gm-spring" data-set="{&quot;rev&quot;:0}"><p><b>A pluck, dry.</b> Reverb at 0. Listen: short and close.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="gm-spring"><p><b>Spring reverb.</b> Reverb mix at 6. Listen: a splashy, boingy space.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="gm-hp" data-set="{&quot;hpOn&quot;:false}"><p><b>Low-pass only.</b> Listen: full bass.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="gm-hp"><p><b>High-pass patched in.</b> Listen: the low end is cut away.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="gm-hp" data-set="{&quot;res&quot;:8}"><p><b>More resonance.</b> Listen: a ringing peak.</p></div>
```

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What is special about the Grandmother&#x27;s reverb?</b></p><ul><li>It is a real spring</li><li>It is digital</li><li>It is a room</li><li>It has none</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual PDF p. 21.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Can it save sounds?</b></p><ul><li>No: you draw them on sheets</li><li>Yes, 1000 of them</li><li>Only drums</li><li>Only on tape</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Semi-modular means…</b></p><ul><li>It plays without cables, and cables can change it</li><li>It has no knobs</li><li>It needs a computer</li><li>It is a drum machine</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>How many keys?</b></p><ul><li>25</li><li>32</li><li>61</li><li>88</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
